title: Engineering Trivia
tagline: Slider-based estimation trivia — 40 numbers every engineer should carry
hub_blurb: Estimate forty engineering quantities on linear and logarithmic scales, then see how well your numerical intuition is calibrated.
card_blurb: Game-show estimation trivia: drag a slider to guess 40 numbers every engineer should carry — yield strengths, ampacities, psi per foot — scored by how close your gut gets, with log-scale sliders for the order-of-magnitude questions. Solo or pass-and-play teams.
description: **Engineering Trivia (Should Have Known That)** — slider-based estimation trivia game for engineering students, in three stages: Linear estimates (35 questions, percent-error scored), Log estimates (5 order-of-magnitude questions), and a Debrief comparing the two. 40 values across Statics & Mechanics, Materials, Electrical, Fluids & Thermo, and Everyday Engineering, each re-sourced to a primary or primary-adjacent citation whose page contains the number, with 23 of the 40 carrying an on-screen qualifier (typical value, range, specified minimum, or code-dependent) so a single number never teaches false precision, and 11 scored against a stated range so the more careful answer is never penalised. Animated guess-vs-truth reveal with a one-line "you should have known that because..." anchor for every number. Solo or 2–4 team pass-and-play with editable names and a running scoreboard. Single self-contained built file, phone-first, works offline; the question bank plus its sourcing metadata lives in `src/data.js` for instructors to edit.
